chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) in his prayer. He said, 'He has no prayer unless he begins with it in a loud or quiet manner.' I said, 'Which is more beloved to you if he is fearful or in a hurry: to recite a chapter or the Opening of the Book?' He said, 'The Opening of the Book.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one does not recite Al-Fatiha, and which recitation is preferred in haste?
ai.summary: Reported in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Al-Ala’ ibn Rustam, this hadith clarifies the juristic consensus that omitting Al-Fatiha invalidates the prayer unless it is recited, emphasizing its status as the 'Mother of the Book' (Umm al-Kitab). It further establishes a practical hierarchy for times of necessity, such as fear or haste, where reciting Al-Fatiha takes precedence over other surahs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the obligatory nature of this specific recitation in every unit of prayer. This ruling underscores the theological view that Al-Fatiha is not merely recommended but essential for the structural validity of Salah.
